title: Saying the opposite
goal: Recognize and use irony, understatement and teasing, and read a humorous column.

intro.text: Irony says the reverse of what it means: *Erken geldin!* to someone two hours late. Understatement says less (*Fena değil* for very good), and teasing runs from friendly *takılmak* to the sharper *laf sokmak* and *iğnelemek*.

vocab.en: to tease (with the dative: bana takılma)
to make a dig, a pointed remark (at someone: dative)
to needle, to make barbed remarks
to take offence (alınma: don't take it badly)
quick-witted, never lost for a reply

exercises.title: Düşünceli komşum
exercises.passage:
Benim çok düşünceli (!) bir komşum var. Arabasını her sabah benim garajımın önüne park ediyor; herhâlde garajım yalnız kalmasın diye. Dün sabah kapıyı açınca yine onun arabasını gördüm. Ne güzel, dedim kendi kendime, bugün de işe erken gidemeyeceğim.

Kapısını çaldım. “Arabanızı çeker misiniz?” dedim. “Hemen, hemen!” dedi ve yarım saat sonra çıktı. Ben de en tatlı sesimle “Hiç acele etmeyin, ben zaten işe geç kalmayı çok severim.” dedim. Bunun üzerine bana uzun uzun özür diledi; fena değil, on dakika daha kaybettim.

Akşam eve dönünce kapımın önünde bir gül ve bir not buldum: “Sabah için kusura bakmayın.” Gülü aldım ve güldüm. Yarın sabah ona ben de bir gül bırakacağım: dikenlisinden.
exercises.translation: I have a very thoughtful (!) neighbour. Every morning he parks his car in front of my garage, presumably so that my garage won't feel lonely. Yesterday morning, when I opened the door, I saw his car again. How nice, I said to myself, I won't get to work early today either. I knocked on his door. 'Could you move your car?' I said. 'Right away, right away!' he said, and came out half an hour later. In my sweetest voice I said: 'Don't hurry at all, I just love being late for work.' At that he apologized at great length: not bad, I lost another ten minutes. When I came home in the evening I found a rose and a note at my door: 'Sorry about this morning.' I took the rose and laughed. Tomorrow morning I'll leave him a rose too: a thorny one.

questions.q: What does the (!) after *düşünceli* tell you?
options: The word is spelled in an unusual way
questions.explain: TDK's spelling guide puts (!) after a word meant ironically.

options: Ben zaten işe geç kalmayı çok severim.
Kapımın önünde bir gül ve bir not buldum.
questions.explain: Nobody loves being late: exaggerated patience that means **hurry up**.

questions.q: What is the play on words in *Gülü aldım ve güldüm*?
What does the writer promise in the last line?
options: A rose of the thorny kind: a friendly dig
To park in front of the neighbour's garage
questions.explain: *Dikenlisinden*: one of the thorny ones. A tease, not a threat.

exercises.question: Your friend arrives two hours late. Which reply is ironic?
exercises.explain: *Erken geldin!* says the reverse of the facts, and the situation makes the meaning clear: you're very late.

exercises.en: Don't be cross, I'm teasing you, I'm joking.
exercises.explain: Only *takılmak* is friendly; *laf sokmak* and *iğnelemek* sting. Note the cases: *sana takılıyorum*, *sana laf sokuyorum*, but *seni iğneliyorum*.

exercises.prompt: Don't take offence, I'm only teasing you.
exercises.explain: *Alınma* is the negative imperative of *alınmak*, to take offence; *takılmak* with the dative is friendly teasing.

exercises.question: Which of these is understatement?
options: *Bin kere söyledim!* (said for the third time)

why.1: Exaggeration: three times becomes a thousand.
why.2: Irony: the reverse of the facts.

exercises.explain: Understatement says less than the truth: *biraz serin* for bitter cold, *fena değil* for very good.

exercises.en: Well done, you've forgotten the key again.

accept: He made a dig at me in the meeting.
He made a dig at me at the meeting
He made a dig at me during the meeting
He took a dig at me [in|at|during] the meeting
He had a dig at me [in|at|during] the meeting
She [made|took|had] a dig at me [in|at|during] the meeting
[He|She] made a [pointed|snide|barbed|sarcastic] remark [to|at|about] me [in|at|during] the meeting
[In|At|During] the meeting [he|she] [made|took|had] a dig at me
[He|She] got a dig in at me [in|at|during] the meeting
exercises.explain: *Laf sokmak*, literally to stick a word in, is a pointed remark at the right moment; the person gets the dative, *bana*.

exercises.task: A friend has burned dinner and asks *Nasıl olmuş?* Answer in two or three sentences of Turkish: first with irony, then kindly, so that the teasing doesn't hurt.
models: Ne güzel olmuş, tam kömür gibi! Şaka şaka, alınma, sana takılıyorum. Hadi, birlikte makarna yapalım.
Hiç fena değil, sadece biraz fazla pişmiş. Takılıyorum, kızma; eline sağlık, düşünmen bile yeter.
checklist: One ironic or understated line: praise that means the opposite, or *biraz fazla pişmiş*
A kind line at the end: thanks, or an offer to help

exercises.en: I took the rose and laughed.
